caseno: Criminal Petition for leave to appeal No. 29 of 2001
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate (with the leave of the Court) instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record, ------ for the Petitioner. 
Respondent : ------ Not represented.
parties:
Most. Sharifa Begum alias Sharu Bibi
Vs.
The State
full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal by the petitioner in jail Most. Sharifa Begum is against the judgment passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5723 of 1999 discharging the Rule and confirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat, Narail, registered as Nari-O-Shishu Case No. 14 of 1998. 

 2. The prosecution case was that the in-formant's younger sister Monowara Begum, aged about 20 years, a divorcee used to reside in her father's house. On 12.6.1996 the convict petitioner came to the informant's fathers house and after talking with her relative Abdul Motaleb took the informant's younger sister with promise that she would provide employment to her. Thereafter there was no information regarding Monowara and on inquiry it was found that the convict petitioner and another had sold victim Monowara in Khizirpur in Calcutta for a large sum of money. The above case was started and court framed charge against the convict petitioner under section 8 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995. Prosecution examined 12 P.Ws. who were all cross-examined by the defence. The convict petitioner was found guilty of the offence charged and convicted her thereunder the sentenced to imprisonment for life and also order to pay a fine of Tk. 5,000/- in default to offer three months rigorous imprisonment more in the aforementioned Nari-O-Shishu Case No. 14 of 1998. The convict petitioner then moved the miscellaneous petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the impugned judgment. It was submitted before the High Court Division that it was a case of no evidence inasmuch as the allegation so brought against the convict petitioner was not sustainable in law. It was further submitted the trial court failed to sift the evidence on record and arrived at a decision on surmise and convicted the petitioner with-out any legal evidence. 

 3. The High Court Division found from the record that the entire proceeding was concluded in the presence of the convict petitioner and. the petition for quashment was filed long after 110 days from the date of judgment Section. 24 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995, provides for filing of appeal against the judgment and order of conviction within 30 days of the date of judgment and it being a special law and there being no provision of getting any benefit under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the proceeding before the High Court Division was barred by limitation. The High Court Division after going through the evidence on record found that the statements of the victim recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was corroborated on dock on material particular points which was inconformity with the provisions of section 8 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 and therefore did not accept the contention that the prosecution had not be able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The petition filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure having been filed long after 110 days of passing of the impugned judgment and victim herself and other p.ws. having corroborated the allegations brought against the convict petitioner and the entire proceeding having taken place in her presence there was no reason to hold that she was not aware of the judgment and order of conviction within time. There was in the petition which brought the case within purview under section 561A for the purpose of Quashment of the proceedings. The High Court Division therefore discharged the Rule.
